summary: 146 ways to say something without finding the words, grouped by intent and linked to the feelings tracker.
invariants: NOT an emoji picker. A phone keyboard already has every emoji; what it lacks is a set organised by what you are trying to SAY, searchable by meaning rather than Unicode name.
EVERY entry carries words. That is the alt text, the search index, and what makes the set usable by someone who reads emoji differently. An emoji without words is a guess at both ends.
every entry maps to feelings, so sending one can set your feeling — but only when asked. Sending a heart is not always a declaration about your internal state.

§12.2 reuse is distinguished from duplication: the same emoji meaning a DIFFERENT thing is deliberate (🫂 is both "holding you" and "I need to be held"). The same emoji meaning the same thing twice is a mistake, and there are none.
the wanting group is hidden in solo mode — nothing is sent to nobody
this is not only a romance set: hard, friction, need and everyday groups carry as much weight
"Something else" is always last, routed through the choice primitive — the private one that means something only between two people is where the real vocabulary lives
